item.title: Oscar-winning producer Gerald R Molen passes away at 91
item.description: Gerald R Molen, the Oscar-winning Hollywood producer known for his association with filmmaker Steven Spielberg and films such as ‘Schindler’s List’, ‘Jurassic Park’ and ‘Minority Report’, has died at ...
item.content:encoded:
Oscar-winning producer Gerald R Molen passes away at 91 Gerald R Molen, the Oscar-winning Hollywood producer known for his association with filmmaker Steven Spielberg and films such as ‘Schindler’s List’, ‘Jurassic Park’ and ‘Minority Report’, has died at the age of 91, according to The Hollywood Reporter. ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 10:10 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 10:10 IST

Late producer Gerald R Molen with director Steven Spielberg and Branko Lustig (Photo/Reuters) . Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Gerald R Molen, the Oscar-winning Hollywood producer known for his association with filmmaker Steven Spielberg and films such as ‘Schindler’s List’, ‘Jurassic Park’ and ‘Minority Report’, has died at the age of 91, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Molen, a longtime resident of Bigfork, Montana, died on Monday, his great-niece Rachel Lorraine Pullan announced. The veteran producer shared the Best Picture Academy Award for Spielberg's ‘Schindler’s List’ (1993) with the filmmaker and Branko Lustig. Molen first collaborated with Spielberg as a unit production manager on ‘The Color Purple’ (1985). The filmmaker subsequently offered him his first producing assignment as an associate producer on “Batteries Not Included” (1987), according to The Hollywood Reporter. After working as a producer on Spielberg's ‘Hook’ (1991), Molen was appointed head of production at Amblin Entertainment, where he oversaw several projects, including ‘The Flintstones’ (1994), ‘The Little Rascals’ (1994), ‘Little Giants’ (1994), ‘Casper’ (1995), 'Twister' (1996) and ‘The Lost World: Jurassic Park’ (1997). Recalling his experience working at Amblin Entertainment in a 2023 interview, Molen said, “It was the best job in Hollywood, because any movie Spielberg directed I got to produce, and any movie the company did I got to oversee,” according to The Hollywood Reporter. Apart from his association with Spielberg and Amblin, Molen also produced several notable films, including the Best Picture Oscar winner ‘Rain Man’ (1988), ‘Days of Thunder’ (1990), ‘The Other Side of Heaven’ (2001), ‘Just Like Heaven’ (2005), ‘The Meg’ (2018) and ‘Meg 2: The Trench’ (2023). Born Gerald Robert Molen on January 6, 1935, in Great Falls, Montana, he moved with his family to North Hollywood in 1947. His parents, Gerald Sr. and Edith, later established a cafe across the street from Republic Pictures in Studio City. Speaking about his early fascination with filmmaking in a 2014 interview, Molen recalled how studio guards would allow him onto the film sets. “I got to make friends with the studio guards,” he said. “They used to take me on the studio lot and take me to a soundstage or the backlot where they were maybe shooting a Western and stuff me down behind a bale of hay or under a wagon. I got it in my blood.” After completing high school, Molen enlisted in the United States Marine Corps. Following 10 months of service, he joined Republic Pictures in 1957 as a truck driver, transporting furniture, according to The Hollywood Reporter. He moved to Universal Studios in 1959 and also had an early on-screen association with Alfred Hitchcock's ‘Psycho’ (1960). Molen doubled for actor Anthony Perkins in a scene featuring a car travelling towards the Bates Motel, with Hitchcock himself seated in the back seat giving directions. Molen subsequently rose to become head of transportation at Universal. Working as a transportation coordinator, captain and supervisor, he was associated with films such as ‘Escape to Witch Mountain’ (1975), ‘Bound for Glory’ (1976), ‘Coming Home’(1978), ‘Being There’ (1979), ‘Ordinary People’ (1980) and ‘Absence of Malice’ (1981). He later transitioned into unit production management, working on ‘The Postman Always Rings Twice’ (1981), ‘Tootsie’ (1982), ‘A Soldier’s Story’ (1984) and Spielberg's ‘The Color Purple’, before establishing himself as a film producer. Molen also made cameo appearances in several films, including ‘Rain Man’, ‘Days of Thunder’, ‘Jurassic Park’, ‘Amistad’ (1997) and ‘Catch Me If You Can’ (2002), the latter two directed by Spielberg. In addition to mainstream Hollywood productions, Molen produced the political documentaries ‘2016: Obama’s America’ (2012) and ‘Hillary’s America: The Secret History of the Democratic Party’(2016). Both films were written and directed by Dinesh D’Souza and were critical of Barack Obama and Hillary Clinton. With a career spanning several decades, Molen remained associated with some of Hollywood's notable productions, particularly through his long-running professional collaboration with Spielberg, according to The Hollywood Reporter. (ANI)

item.title: Iran vows to break US naval blockade, claims full control over Strait of Hormuz: MP Esmaeil Kowsari
item.description: Iran has vowed to break the US naval blockade through the capabilities of its armed forces, with Iranian MP Esmaeil Kowsari claiming that Tehran exercises "full control" over the strategically ...
item.content:encoded:
Iran vows to break US naval blockade, claims full control over Strait of Hormuz: MP Esmaeil Kowsari Iran has vowed to break the US naval blockade through the capabilities of its armed forces, with Iranian MP Esmaeil Kowsari claiming that Tehran exercises "full control" over the strategically important Strait of Hormuz and warning against any foreign military intervention targeting the country. ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 09:55 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 09:55 IST

Representative Image (FilePhoto/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Iran

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Iran has vowed to break the US naval blockade through the capabilities of its armed forces, with Iranian MP Esmaeil Kowsari claiming that Tehran exercises "full control" over the strategically important Strait of Hormuz and warning against any foreign military intervention targeting the country. Speaking on Iran's state broadcaster IRIB, a member of the National Security and Foreign Policy Commission of the Iranian Parliament, Kowsari, said the country's military had been preparing to secure control over the strategic waterway since 1987. He maintained that Iran would not allow its adversaries to gain access or establish influence over the Strait of Hormuz, adding that the country's missile and drone capabilities had altered the military calculations of the United States in the region. “The US naval blockade will be broken by the strategies and capabilities of Iran's armed forces, and the timing and method of responding to enemy actions are at the discretion of the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran,” Kowsari said. Attributing the withdrawal of American warships from the region to Iran's military capabilities, he said the country's strategic strength extended beyond its energy resources and included its ability to influence developments in the Strait of Hormuz. Kowsari also cautioned neighbouring countries against allowing their territory or military infrastructure to be used for operations targeting Iran, warning that such cooperation would carry consequences. "Any country that provides its capabilities and territory to the United States for action against Iran will be responsible for the consequences, and the use of European airspace to attack Iran will not go unanswered by the Islamic Republic," he said. He further warned that disruptions to commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could impose high economic costs on countries across the region. Clarifying Tehran's military position, Kowsari said Iran did not seek to initiate a war or prolong the ongoing conflict but remained prepared to respond decisively to any aggression. He added that removing foreign military forces from the region and holding those responsible for attacks accountable remained among Iran's objectives. The remarks come amid continuing tensions between Washington and Tehran, with US President Donald Trump claiming that victory in the conflict with Iran was within reach while indicating that his administration was offering Tehran an opportunity to negotiate an agreement. Speaking during a Thanksgiving call with US military personnel from his Mar-a-Lago residence in Florida, Trump said the timing of an American victory would depend on his decision. "We have victory at hand [in Iran]. It will happen whenever I want it to happen. We are trying to be nice. We are giving them every chance to make a deal and save a lot of lives, but I am not sure if they are going to take advantage of that," Trump said. Meanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said Tehran's immediate priority was strengthening the country's resilience against external pressure while ensuring the uninterrupted movement of trade and essential supplies. Araghchi said diplomatic efforts were continuing, with Qatar and Pakistan maintaining mediation channels and conveying proposals between the concerned parties. He added that negotiations remained part of Iran's approach but that countering external pressure was currently a key priority. The Iranian Foreign Minister also accused Israel of attempting to create an atmosphere conducive to renewed military confrontation and draw Washington into another conflict with Tehran. Reiterating Iran's position, Araghchi said the country remained prepared to defend itself while keeping diplomatic channels open, provided its demands were respected. (ANI)

item.title: India's non-alcoholic beverage market to grow 13% annually to Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30: Report
item.description: India's non-alcoholic ready-to-drink beverage market is expected to grow at around 13 per cent annually to reach Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30, driven by rising demand for energy drinks, protein-based ...
item.content:encoded:
India's non-alcoholic beverage market to grow 13% annually to Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30: Report India's non-alcoholic ready-to-drink beverage market is expected to grow at around 13 per cent annually to reach Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30, driven by rising demand for energy drinks, protein-based beverages and advanced hydration products, according to a Dolat Capital report. ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 09:50 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 09:50 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India's non-alcoholic ready-to-drink beverage market is expected to grow at around 13 per cent annually to reach Rs 2.56 lakh crore by FY30, driven by rising demand for energy drinks, protein-based beverages and advanced hydration products, according to a Dolat Capital report. The market, estimated at Rs 1.40 lakh crore in FY26, is seeing a shift beyond traditional refreshment towards products offering additional health and functional benefits. Energy drinks and advanced hydration solutions are expected to grow at more than twice the overall industry rate, prompting consumer goods companies to expand their presence in these segments. According to the report, energy drinks are projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 25.6 per cent between FY26 and FY31, while advanced hydration products are expected to expand at 30.2 per cent. Their respective market sizes are estimated to rise from Rs 9,300 crore and Rs 4,200 crore in FY26 to Rs 29,000 crore and Rs 15,800 crore by FY30. The report noted that "Protein is moving from supplements to everyday beverage", with companies extending protein-based products beyond traditional nutrition supplements to ready-to-drink options for regular consumers. Hydration products are also moving beyond packaged drinking water. HUL and Tata Consumer have entered the advanced hydration segment with products aimed at sports, electrolyte replenishment and recovery. The report also highlighted growing demand for low-sugar alternatives, with companies introducing zero-sugar beverage variants. Varun Beverages has launched Ad Rush in the mid-priced energy drink segment and Evervess in premium mixers as part of its portfolio expansion. Beyond beverages, consumer companies are also focusing on protein-rich foods, convenient ready-to-eat products and ingredient-led personal care offerings. Dolat Capital said these launches reflect a broader shift towards health-focused products, premium offerings and new consumption categories, as companies look to expand beyond their traditional businesses. (ANI)

item.title: Danny Boyle backs Jack O’Connell as James Bond villain, says actor "would have been a great 007"
item.description: Filmmaker Danny Boyle has backed actor Jack O’Connell as a potential villain in the upcoming James Bond film, while maintaining that the actor would also have been a strong choice to play the iconic ...
item.content:encoded:
Danny Boyle backs Jack O’Connell as James Bond villain, says actor "would have been a great 007" Filmmaker Danny Boyle has backed actor Jack O’Connell as a potential villain in the upcoming James Bond film, while maintaining that the actor would also have been a strong choice to play the iconic British spy, according to Variety.  ANI | Updated: 27-11-2026 09:47 IST | Created: 27-11-2026 09:47 IST

Danny Boyle (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Filmmaker Danny Boyle has backed actor Jack O’Connell as a potential villain in the upcoming James Bond film, while maintaining that the actor would also have been a strong choice to play the iconic British spy, according to Variety. Boyle, who previously starred O’Connell in his film “Ink”, said there had been growing speculation about the actor taking on the antagonist’s role opposite Robert Pattinson, who has been cast as the next James Bond. Speaking on the Alchemy with Anthony Mason podcast, the filmmaker praised both O’Connell and Pattinson for their screen presence, saying they possess an elusive quality that makes audiences want to watch them. “They have that thing where you want to watch them,” Boyle said. “And it’s impossible to quantify what it is, otherwise we’d all buy it for ourselves. But it’s just there, and you want to follow them.” However, Boyle also acknowledged that O’Connell could have been an excellent choice for the lead role, adding that the actor “would have been a great Bond as well," according to Variety. O’Connell was previously believed to have been among the actors considered for the coveted role of 007. Interestingly, Boyle had also expressed support for Pattinson as a potential James Bond years before the actor was reportedly selected for the role. In 2019, after stepping away from directing “No Time to Die” over creative differences, Boyle suggested that Pattinson could replace Daniel Craig as the next 007. At the time, Boyle was particularly impressed by Pattinson's performance in Claire Denis' science-fiction film “High Life”. Speaking in an interview in 2019, he recalled thinking, “It was so bizarre, because I was sitting there thinking: ‘Oh my God, they should get him to be the next Bond.’” Reflecting on Pattinson's casting, Boyle said he had recognised the actor's star potential much earlier, including during his performances in the “Twilight” films. “He’s a movie star, and I could see that from the first ‘Twilight’ films. Him and Kristen Stewart, the two of them. You thought: they’re movie stars. It’s like a given,” he said, according to Variety. “So there’s not that many of them out there. And having a British pedigree will always help him in that world as well,” Boyle added. Boyle was originally attached to direct the 25th James Bond film, “No Time to Die”, but exited the project in 2018 following creative differences with the producers. The film was eventually directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga, with Daniel Craig returning as 007, according to Variety. With Pattinson now set to take on the iconic role, Boyle's latest remarks have also brought renewed attention to O’Connell as a potential addition to the Bond franchise, this time on the other side of the battle. (ANI)
